title: Deere Q3 2026 Earnings Preview: DE Revenue, Guidance, Margins
summary: Deere & Company (DE) Q3 2026 earnings preview: modest revenue growth, margin pressures, and segment performance insights.
body_text: Deere & Company (DE) — Q3 2026 Earnings Preview Key Preview Table: What to Watch for in Q3 2026 Factor Q3 2026E (Consensus) Q3 2025 Actual YoY Change Q2 2026 Actual Sequential Trend Guidance/Context Notes Revenue ( $M ) $10,766 $10,327 +4% $11,495 -6% Guidance: FY26 $4.5B–$5.0B net income; Q3 typically seasonally lower than Q2 Gross Profit Margin (%) 26.8 27.9 -110 bps 28.6 -180 bps Margins pressured by tariffs, input costs; Q2 margin benefited from one-time tariff refund EBITDA ( $M ) $1,938 $1,849 +5% $2,320 -16% EBITDA margin expected to compress YoY and sequentially Net Income ( $M ) $1,257 $1,223 +3% $1,553 -19% Guidance: FY26 $4.5B–$5.0B; Q3 typically below Q2, above Q1 EPS (GAAP) $4.73 $4.59 +3% $5.74 -18% EPS tracks net income; Q2 benefited from tariff refund Cash Flow per Share ($) $14.23 $6.53 +118% $10.04 +42% Strong cash flow YTD; Q3 typically strong on working capital release Equipment Ops Margin (%) 16.9 Q2 margin boosted by tariff refund; Q3 expected to normalize Segment Revenue Growth See segment table below Segment Revenue & Margin Preview — Q3 2026E Segment Q3 2026E Revenue ( $M ) Q3 2025 Actual ( $M ) YoY Growth Q2 2026 Actual ( $M ) Q3 2026E Margin (%) Q3 2025 Margin (%) Guidance/Notes Production & Precision Ag $4,273 $4,503 11–13 (FY guide) 13.6 Down 5–10% FY26; Q3 likely down YoY Small Ag & Turf $3,025 $3,485 13.5–15 (FY guide) 16.0 Up ~15% FY26; Q3 likely up YoY Construction & Forestry $3,059 $3,790 10–12 (FY guide) 7.7 Up ~20% FY26; Q3 likely up YoY Note: Segment-level Q3 2026 consensus not available; use Q2 2026 actuals and FY guidance as directional indicators. Summary and Conclusions Q3 2026 is expected to show modest YoY growth in revenue and net income, with consensus forecasting revenue of $10.8B (+4% YoY) and net income of $1.26B (+3% YoY). Margins are under pressure YoY and sequentially due to ongoing tariff headwinds, higher input costs, and a less favorable mix, especially in large ag. Q2 2026 benefited from a one-time $272M tariff refund, which will not repeat in Q3; expect margins to normalize lower. Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry segments are expected to drive growth, offsetting continued weakness in Production & Precision Ag (large ag), which remains below trough levels. Management has maintained FY26 net income guidance at $4.5B–$5.0B, signaling confidence in the full-year outlook despite volatility in ag markets and global macro uncertainty. Key focus areas for Q3: pace of recovery in large ag, sustainability of margin improvement in Small Ag & Turf and C&F, price realization vs. cost inflation, and any updates on order books/inventory trends. Recent Results and Year-over-Year Comparison Q3 2025 Actuals (Restated Where Available) Metric Q3 2025 Actual Revenue ( $M ) $10,327 Gross Profit Margin 27.9% EBITDA ( $M ) $1,849 Net Income ( $M ) $1,223 EPS (GAAP) $4.59 Cash Flow/Share ($) $6.53 Q3 2025 was a down quarter YoY, with revenue -9% and net income -26% vs. Q3 2024. Production & Precision Ag sales were down 16% YoY, Small Ag & Turf down 1%, and Construction & Forestry down 5%. Margins were pressured by tariffs and negative price realization, especially in large ag and C&F. Company was coming off a tough comparable in large ag, with industry sales down ~30% in North America. Forward Guidance and Consensus FY26 Guidance (as of Q2 2026) Metric FY26 Guidance Notes Net Income ( $B ) $4.5–$5.0 Unchanged since Q1; midpoint $4.75B Equipment Ops Cash Flow ( $B ) $4.5–$5.5 Raised by $500M at both ends in Q1 Effective Tax Rate (%) 24–26 Lowered by 1pt vs. prior due to mix/discrete items PPA Net Sales Growth Down 5–10% Price +1%, FX +3% (Q2 update) SAT Net Sales Growth Up ~15% Price +1.5%, FX +1% (Q2 update) C&F Net Sales Growth Up ~20% Price +2.5%, FX +2% (Q2 update) PPA Margin (%) 11–13 Unchanged SAT Margin (%) 13.5–15 Unchanged C&F Margin (%) 10–12 Raised in Q2 Tariff Expense ( $B ) ~$1.2 $900M net after Q2 refund; 3% margin headwind Financial Services NI ( $M ) ~$860 Raised in Q2 Management Commentary and Intra-Quarter Color On Market Conditions and Segment Trends: Large Ag: "Customer sentiment remains muted... margins face headwinds from elevated and volatile input costs and high interest rates." (Q2 2026 call) Small Ag & Turf: "Benefiting from a recovery in turf end markets and healthy cash flow in the dairy and livestock sector." Construction & Forestry: "Robust infrastructure spending and rental fleet replacement are driving increased demand... order book continues to strengthen up more than 60% since November." On Margins and Tariffs: "Q2 margin benefited from a one-time $272M IEEPA tariff refund, lifting margins by nearly 2.5 points. Net of refunds, full-year direct tariff exposure remains at ~$1.2B." "Implied net price realization for equipment operations is between 1.5% and 2% for the year, consistent with general inflation levels, excluding the impact of tariffs." "We are not surcharging our customers on tariffs... focusing on reducing our tariff exposure through cost actions." On Inventory and Order Books: "Inventories for both high horsepower tractors and combines are down more than 50% from their mid-2024 peak." "Order books remain healthy and consistent with our retail-driven production plans." "Within Small Ag & Turf in North America, favorable inventory levels are being maintained, following last year's under production." On Innovation and Product Launches: "Launched multiple new products and solutions to strengthen our leadership across each major step of the ag production cycle." "See & Spray technology continues to advance... globally, it was 5 million acres last year; early in the spring season, customers are spraying more acres than last year." "Precision Essentials renewal rate is over 90% for the second-year cohort." What to Watch for in Q3 2026 Revenue and Margin Progression: Can Deere maintain positive YoY growth in revenue and net income despite ongoing large ag weakness and margin headwinds? Tariff Impact: How does the absence of the Q2 one-time tariff refund affect Q3 margins? Is the company making further progress on tariff mitigation? Segment Performance: Will Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry continue to offset large ag softness? Are segment margins holding up? Order Book and Inventory Trends: Any signs of inflection in large ag demand/order books? Is inventory discipline sustained? Price Realization vs. Cost Inflation: Is price/cost neutral or positive in Q3? Are there further pressures from input/freight/materials costs? Technology Adoption: Updates on See & Spray, Precision Essentials, and other tech adoption/utilization rates. FY26 Guidance: Any change to the $4.5B–$5.0B net income range or segment outlooks? Conclusion Deere enters Q3 2026 with a stable but cautious outlook. The company is coming off a tough comparable in large ag but is seeing strength in Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry. Margins are under pressure from tariffs and input costs, and the Q2 one-time tariff refund will not repeat. The most important factors for Q3 are the sustainability of margin improvement, the pace of recovery in large ag, and the ability to offset cost headwinds with price and operational execution. Guidance remains unchanged, and management continues to emphasize inventory discipline, innovation, and long-term growth targets.

title: Polymath Robotics Blog | Meet Kai: The AI-Powered Humanoid Robot for Heavy Industry
summary: Polymath announces our new humanoid robot for heavy industry.
body_text: Polymath Robotics is proud to introduce Kai, a cutting-edge humanoid robot poised to transform heavy industry. Named for its "Knowledge AI" capabilities, Kai offers unmatched versatility and efficiency. Our CEO Stefan Seltz-Axmacher remarked, when we reached him on the bridge of his boat, "Once we realized how good humanoids are at locomotion and fine motor skills, we shifted focus immediately from automating vehicles to developing Kai. After all, why automate the vehicle when you can automate the driver?" ‍ Concept art for KAI, the modern industrial humanoid Kai has a wide range of industrial applications including agriculture, construction, and modern dance. CTO Ilia Baranov adds "I've always said: 'Why legs?' But when I saw what Kai could do, I said, 'Yes, legs. Definitely legs.'" What separates Kai from other impressive humanoid projects is its sophistication. "A superhuman amount of engineering has gone into Kai," Stefan notes, emphasizing that Kai is "definitely NOT our intern in a robot suit." Preorders from major construction, mining, and traveling dance troupes highlight Kai's industry-wide appeal. Most important, however, is the impressive demo we showcased live on our TikTok, of Kai performing its signature moves: Happy April Fools :)

body_text: View All News Hexcel Announces Expanded Long-Term Agreements with Boeing July 20, 2026 Download (opens in new window) FARNBOROUGH, England--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Hexcel Corporation (NYSE: HXL), a global leader in advanced lightweight composites technology, announced a series of new and extended long-term agreements with The Boeing Company, reinforcing the companies’ collaboration across commercial, defense and space programs. “These agreements reflect the strength of our partnership with Boeing and our shared commitment to advancing composite technology in aerospace applications,” said Lyndon Smith, President, Americas & Global Fibers, Hexcel. “We are well positioned to support current production demands while developing solutions that address the industry’s future performance and sustainability needs. We remain focused on supporting Boeing’s production priorities while contributing to innovation across its aircraft portfolio.” The agreements include a broad enterprise-level composite material supply framework and a key contract extension supporting Boeing’s advanced acoustic engineered core needs for engine applications, further positioning Hexcel to deliver high-performance materials across critical aerospace systems. These long-term agreements expand Hexcel’s role as a key materials supplier across Boeing’s major platforms while strengthening long-term supply and technology alignment between the companies. About Hexcel Hexcel Corporation Hexcel Corporation is a global leader in advanced lightweight composites technology. We provide innovative, high-performance material solutions that are lighter, stronger, and tougher, shaping a world that moves farther, smarter, and more efficiently. Our broad and unrivaled product range includes carbon fiber, specialty reinforcements, prepregs and other fiber-reinforced matrix materials, honeycomb, resins, engineered core, and composite structures for use in commercial aerospace, defense and space, and industrial applications. title: IDEX Health & Science Introduces New Constant Performance Degassing Pump System
summary: Our New Constant Performance Vacuum Degassing Pump allows for variable vacuum levels based on your preferred method flow rate.
body_text: Rohnert Park, California, August 28, 2020 — IDEX Health & Science (IH&S), industry leader in fluidic components and subsystems, introduces a new Constant Performance Degassing Pump (CPDP) system that enables a new method of in-line HPLC degassing control that delivers greater HPLC instrument performance and reliability. This new method of in-line HPLC degassing control is made possible by IDEX Health & Science’s latest dual stage pump and an integrated microprocessor control that characterizes the efficiency of a new, high performance Film Degasser at various applied vacuum levels. The resulting calibration data produces a mathematical model of degassing channel performance that allows the HPLC system to operate the vacuum degasser at the highest possible pressure (minimal vacuum level) to degas with minimal mobile phase concentration changes and reduced solvent loss to the laboratory atmosphere. “This intelligent, user interactive control system with patent-pending algorithm when used with our Film Degasser, will provide more performance, increased efficiency and tighter control for HPLC instrument precision & reliability”, said Saba Jazeeli Sr. Product Manager, Analytical Instrument Market. For more information about the new Constant Performance Degassing Pump System, visit: www.idex-hs.com/store/fluidics/degassers/vacuum-control-system.html For more information about the Film Degasser, visit: www.idex-hs.com/store/fluidics/degassers/film-degasser.html About IDEX Health & Science LLC IDEX Health & Science LLC is the global leader in life science fluidics, microfluidics, and optics, offering a three-fold advantage to customers by bringing optofluidic paths to life with strategic partnerships, solutions, and expertise. As one of the few companies in the world with component, sub-system, and application level experts, IDEX Health & Science helps instrument developers solve the most demanding fluidic and optical challenges in a wide array of applications. At IDEX Health & Science we believe partnership will change the way the world innovates, leading to new technologies that improve our health, protect our planet, and enrich our lives. For more information visit: www.idex-hs.com
